title: Interest on Personal Credit Cards: Basis of Computation, Grace and Reversal
content:
### How interest is computed

Interest on Personal Credit Cards is computed by the average daily balance method, including new transactions, separately for the purchase, cash advance, balance transfer and penalty balances, at each balance's own rate divided by a day-count basis of 365, and is billed at statement close as one interest entry per balance type that is above 0.00 USD.

### Grace, and where there is none

Purchases carry a grace period: no purchase interest is billed for a cycle when the prior statement balance was paid in full by its due date. That is so when the payments, merchant credits and dispute credits posted from the prior statement's closing date through that statement's payment due date total at least that prior statement's balance. Otherwise purchase interest accrues from each purchase's posted date. Cash advances accrue from their posted date with no grace period. Balance transfers accrue at the introductory rate through the introductory rate end date and at the purchase rate afterwards.

### The smallest billable charge

When any interest is due for a cycle but the total is below the tier's smallest interest charge, the tier's smallest interest charge is billed instead, allocated to the purchase balance type.

### Reversal of residual interest as a courtesy

Residual interest is interest billed on the statement after the cardholder paid a statement balance in full, for the days between that statement's closing date and the payment date. It may be reversed in full, as a courtesy waiver, up to the tier's allowance of such reversals in a rolling 365 calendar days ending on the day of the decision, counted across all of the customer's cards. A courtesy reversal of residual interest requires that the statement balance it follows was paid in full; that is read from the card's own ledger entries before the reversal is made.

### Reversal for bank error, and the one-reversal rule

Interest billed at a rate or on a balance contrary to this charter is reversed as a bank error, without limit. An interest charge can be reversed at most once: an interest charge already named as the source item of a reversal on that card is not reversed again.

*Points of judgement.* An interest charge of exactly 0.00 USD for a balance type writes no entry, the test being above 0.00 USD. A cycle in which interest is due but totals less than the tier's smallest interest charge is billed at that smallest charge, not at the computed total and not at nothing. Where a customer's courtesy reversals of residual interest in the rolling 365 days already equal the tier's allowance, the allowance is spent; the count is taken across the customer's cards rather than card by card.
